findings.reason: The protected recursive first-child/next-sibling codec raises RecursionError on a legal height-1000 chain. The inert candidate preserves the exact representation, stateless behavior, O(n) time, and O(h) auxiliary bound with explicit continuation frames that pass both legal maxima.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 431 and its Python Codec surface. The app contract explicitly distinguishes the recursive local fixture shape from the native level-order display and returns the reconstructed N-ary Node after the required encode/decode round trip. The Reference preserves the unrestricted codec requirement, all three exact source examples, all four constraints, and the source diagram's complete relationships in an accessible table.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064797983 and remains aligned with the protected app-local recursive codec. The candidate is inert and creates the same binary node per N-ary node, identical left first-child links, and identical ordered right-sibling chains, but uses explicit continuation frames; promotion would still require separately Accepted native evidence.

The legal 64-, 192-, and 512-node star tiers span 8x and isolate sibling-link construction while validating the reconstructed N-ary tree. The candidate passes all 12 black-box executions at +0.02 extra growth and 1.45x the protected reference runtime; a correct control that rescans the right-sibling chain for every append passes every output but fails only the runtime verdict at 21.71x.

The Approach now describes the candidate exactly: left first-child links, right next-sibling chains, parent continuation frames, symmetric decoding continuations, reversibility, stateless calls, O(n) time, and O(h) auxiliary space without interpreter recursion.

The hash-bound Reference was checked against the authenticated live Premium statement. It preserves the statement order, N-ary and binary definitions, level-order null separators, illustrative rather than mandatory encoding, all example literals, every constraint, and the full source-image structure through a locally authored table.

coverage: All three authenticated Premium source examples now appear first and in source order, including the previously missing 14-node tree, with exact ordered structure and empty-tree facts; the invented leaf is correctly labelled a trial.
Visible cases cover empty and single-node trees, values 0 and 10000, chains, wide sibling lists, repeated values, independent branches, and deliberately non-sorted child order.
Generated legal boundaries cover a 10,000-node star and a height-1000 chain, preventing node-count and interpreter-recursion regressions without embedding an unparseably deep JSON fixture.

Independent structural checks verified all nine authored cases, all three benchmarks, 3,000 randomized ordered trees, stateless codec reuse, exact protected/candidate binary representations on overlapping inputs, and both maximum constructions.
All nine correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 64-, 192-, and 512-node sibling-chain workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
